name: The Trust
one_liner: Psychologist malpractice insurance with a choice of occurrence or claims-made coverage and free risk consultations.
short_description: Professional liability insurance built for psychologists and pre-licensure psychology trainees, with occurrence or claims-made forms and the Advocate 800 consult line.
long_description: The Trust (trustinsurance.com) was established by the American Psychological Association in 1962 as a separate legal entity, then known as the APA Insurance Trust; a 2013 restructuring let it sell to psychologists who are not APA members. Its professional liability program covers the practice of psychology for individuals and groups, plus a separate program for pre-licensure psychologists. The program is administered by Trust Risk Management Services and underwritten by ACE American Insurance Company, a Chubb company; The Trust states the carrier holds A.M. Best's top rating. Psychologists can choose occurrence or claims-made coverage, with annual limits up to $2,000,000 per incident and $4,000,000 aggregate, and claims-made policyholders get a free tail on retirement, death or disability. Licensing board defense reimbursement starts at $5,000 with higher options, and first- or third-party cyber coverage can be added to the same policy. Every policyholder has unlimited access to the Advocate 800 program, consultations with licensed psychologists who have legal, ethical and risk-management expertise. Rates and discounts are published on its site and a quick quote is available online.

faqs.q: Is The Trust the same as the APA Insurance Trust?
faqs.a: Yes. It was set up by the American Psychological Association in 1962 as the APA Insurance Trust, a separate legal entity, and now operates as The Trust.

faqs.q: Who underwrites The Trust's professional liability policy?
faqs.a: The program is administered by Trust Risk Management Services and underwritten by ACE American Insurance Company, a Chubb company.

faqs.q: Does The Trust offer occurrence or claims-made coverage?
faqs.a: Both. Psychologists choose the form; claims-made policies include a free tail on retirement, death or disability.
A no-cost consultation service for policyholders with licensed psychologists who have legal, ethical and risk-management expertise.

faqs.q: Is The Trust the American Psychological Association's endorsed program?
faqs.a: No. The Trust operates independently. The American Psychological Association's member insurance page names American Professional Agency, underwritten by Allied World, as the administrator of its professional liability program.
